description: GEER Puebla-Mexico City Earthquake is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Tara Hutchinson, University of California San Diego (ucsd.edu). UNAM-GEER formed a reconnaissance team to investigate and document the geotechnical effects of the Puebla-Mexico City M 7.1 19 September 2017 earthquake in Mexico. Data provided within this project includes specifically LiDAR and UAV point clouds (las and potree files) as well as compiled videos from the teams field survey. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-aetm-8891. Keywords: Earthquake reconnaissance, geotechnical earthquake engineering, site effects, subsidence, site response. Published 2019-07-12. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
